headline: Ivanti's chained Connect Secure zero-days join CISA's exploited catalog as unpatched GitLab servers keep taking RCE attacks
standfirst: CISA has added two Ivanti Connect Secure flaws to its known-exploited catalog after they were chained in zero-day attacks, while more than a thousand internet-exposed GitLab servers remain unpatched against an actively exploited maximum-severity RCE. Also in the file: a 1.3 million-device Android TV botnet, a $6 billion crypto heist attributed to North Korea, Apple's 99-country spyware warnings, an SSN-exposing student-aid breach, remotely sabotaged supermarket freezers, and critical Langflow flaws with no KEV listing.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

Both of the day's CVE IDs sit in one story: Ivanti Connect Secure flaws chained in zero-day attacks and now in CISA's catalog [[s32]]. CVE-2026-111357 is catalogued as a missing-authentication weakness for a critical function and scored 7.0 HIGH (CVSS 3.1, MITRE); NVD's description says the broker's handling of DSCache configuration data lets an attacker escalate to root, and states it has been exploited in the wild. CVE-2026-118527, a predictable-numbers-or-identifiers flaw, has a KEV entry but no NVD record in the supplied evidence, so its severity and affected versions are unknown here. Configuration data for the first flaw covers Connect Secure 25.1.0.0 up to but excluding 25.1.1.3, plus the 22.8 R2 line through R2.5. One inconsistency is worth flagging rather than resolving by convenience: the KEV entry names missing authentication, while the NVD vector is local, high-complexity and low-privilege. CISA's required action is to apply vendor mitigations, follow its risk-based patching guidance, or discontinue the product; the two carry separate federal deadlines, and ransomware use is listed as unknown for both. Analysis: the chaining is the story — an escalation primitive paired with a predictable-identifier flaw is what turns a single appliance bug into an intrusion path — though nothing supplied attributes this to a named actor.

More than 1,000 internet-exposed GitLab servers are still unpatched against a maximum-severity remote code execution flaw under ongoing attack [[s21]]. No CVE ID or version range appears in the supplied excerpt, so identification has to come from the vendor's own advisory; the exposed-instance count is the actionable signal.

## Industry

Google and partners have dismantled XCPE, a botnet of more than 1.3 million Android TV streaming boxes that Google says the manufacturer intentionally infected to earn cybercrime revenue; the manufacturer has been banned [[s3]]. The FBI has attributed the $6 billion Binance hack to North Korea's TraderTraitor and flagged more than 600 addresses as the proceeds are laundered [[s30]]. Apple has warned users in 99 countries of mercenary spyware, declining to name actors or regions and citing the cost, sophistication and worldwide nature of such attacks [[s14]].

## Breaches

The Florida Department of Education says Social Security numbers and other personal data may have been exposed in a breach of its financial aid website, putting data on 4.9 million people at risk [[s13]]. Separately, a cyberattack on refrigeration systems disrupted stores run by multiple supermarket chains across several European countries after attackers remotely changed temperature settings on freezers and cooling systems [[s16]] — Analysis: the supplied facts describe immediate operational disruption rather than data loss, which is the notable part.

## Vulnerabilities

Two critical Langflow flaws could let a remote attacker with no account bypass authentication or run arbitrary code, according to IBM [[s22]]. Every release from 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 is affected and 1.13.0 is the only fix. Neither flaw is listed in CISA's KEV catalog, and the excerpt reports no in-the-wild exploitation — which is a catalog miss, not proof that none has occurred.

selected.title: Ivanti Patches Two More Zero-Days Exploited in Connect Secure Attack Chain
selected.excerpt: CISA has added CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527 to its KEV catalog after the Ivanti VPN flaws were chained in zero-day attacks. The post Ivanti Patches Two More Zero-Days Exploited in Connect Secure Attack Chain appeared first on SecurityWeek.

kev.vulnerabilityName: Ivanti Connect Secure Missing Authentication for Critical Function Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: Ivanti Connect Secure contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability that could allow a local authenticated attacker to escalate their privileges. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-118527.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description: Ivanti Connect Secure 22.8R2.4 mishandles the manner in which the dsinvoked broker trusts DSCache configuration data, leading to privilege escalation to root, as exploited in the wild in October 2026.

kev.vulnerabilityName: Ivanti Connect Secure Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: Ivanti Connect Secure contains a generation of predictable numbers or identifiers vulnerability that allows a remote authenticated attacker to upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-111357.
